additional_concerns: The nav > 0 scope restriction is not stated in the circular. It returns OUT_OF_SCOPE for otherwise covered Funds with non-positive NAV, even when an applicable SFC designation exists. Measurement validity should be distinguished from legal scope.

For positive NAV and exact common valuation units, twice aggregate exposure >= NAV correctly preserves the inclusive 50% threshold. The repeated addition is not itself an erroneous doubling of the threshold.

Footnote 7 places the holistic designation assessment below 50%. Using an actual applicable designation as an alternative classification route preserves that distinction in outcome for positive NAV without implementing the SFC's assessment process.

The representation invokes a supplied exposure methodology, but none is supplied. Applicable measurement authority or SFC clarification is missing; look-through, valuation, netting and overlap treatment remain unresolved. No supplied dependency ID can be reliably assigned to that authority.
Assessment time, reassessment frequency and the consequences of subsequent threshold changes are not specified by the retained circular.
The global CONFLICT policy can block an otherwise independently established classification route. It is an evidentiary runtime convention, not a requirement stated by the circular.
The three unbound dependency IDs have no identifying metadata and have null source hashes. None establishes available authority or a reliable catalogue match.
Classification does not establish compliance with the separate direct-investment limit, disclosure requirements, distributor duties or prevailing complex-product sales requirements.
